papers.title: Qishen Yangxin Granule ameliorates cardiac function and ventricular remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy by attenuating inflammation and myocardial fibrosis.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.authors: Tao S, Yu L, Li J, Zhang Z, Liu Y, Wu J et al.
papers.abstract:
Qishen Yangxin Granule (QSYX), a clinically utilized traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for cardiovascular diseases. However, its cardioprotective mechanism in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains incompletely defined.
To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of QSYX against DCM and the associated anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic mechanisms.
Cardioprotective effects of QSYX were assessed both in vivo using a doxorubicin-induced DCM rat model and in vitro using rat cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. Evaluations included cardiac function, histopathological analysis, levels of inflammatory factors, and myocardial fibrosis markers. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to explore the potential mechanism of QSYX-mediated improvement in cardiac structure and function. Modulation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway was examined via western blot, immunohistochemistry, confocal laser scanning microscope, and real-time reverse transcription-PCR. The specific p38 MAPK agonist LY188011 was used to verify the dependence of QSYX effect on the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.
QSYX administration improved cardiac function in DCM rats, accompanied by significant attenuation of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, apoptosis, inflammatory cell infiltration, and collagen deposition. Comparable protective effects were observed in lipopolysaccharide-treated cardiac fibroblasts. Mechanistically, QSYX suppressed lipopolysaccharide-induced upregulation of TLR4, p38 MAPK, and NF-κB p65 and downregulated the expression of inflammatory factors and myocardial fibrosis markers. Furthermore, intervention with LY188011 confirmed that the cardioprotective effects of QSYX are mediated through suppression of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.
QSYX attenuates myocardial inflammation and fibrosis primarily through inhibition of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby exerting cardioprotective effects against DCM-induced cardiac injury.

summary.question: 기심양심과립이 확장성 심근병증에서 심장 보호 효과를 보이는지와 그 기전을 평가했다.
summary.methods: 독소루비신 유도 DCM 랫드와 LPS 자극 심장 섬유아세포를 이용해 심기능, 조직학, 염증·섬유화 지표를 평가하고 TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB 경로를 분석했다.
summary.results: 기심양심과립은 심기능을 개선하고 염증세포 침윤과 콜라겐 침착을 줄였으며, TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB 신호 억제를 통해 염증과 섬유화를 완화했다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 확장성 심근병증에서 이 한약 처방은 전임상 수준에서 항염·항섬유화 기전을 시사하지만, 임상 적용 전 사람 대상 근거가 더 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 동물 및 세포 실험 중심의 전임상 연구로, 사람에서의 유효성과 안전성은 확인되지 않았다.

papers.title: Thermosensitive in situ nasal gel of Magnoliae Flos-Centipeda Herba for allergic rhinitis: preparation, characterization, and in vivo pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics studies.
papers.journal: Pharmaceutical development and technology
papers.authors: Ma Y, Wang Z, Kang B, Xia Q, Yan H
papers.abstract: Magnoliae Flos and Centipeda Herba are classic herbal medicines for allergic rhinitis in traditional Chinese medicine, yet conventional nasal drops suffer from rapid clearance by nasal mucocilia, leading to limited nasal residence time. Herein, a thermosensitive in situ gel loaded with Magnoliae Flos and Centipeda Herba extract (MFCH-TGL) was fabricated to achieve prolonged, safe intranasal delivery. The gel matrix was composed of 17% (w/v) poloxamer 407 and 1% (w/v) poloxamer 188, incorporated with 2.3% (w/v) alcoholic extract and 0.5% (v/v) volatile oil of MFCH. We systematically characterized sol-gel transition performance, rheological behavior, in vitro release and ex vivo nasal permeation, and further assessed anti-allergic pharmacodynamics in BALB/c mice as well as nasal pharmacokinetics in SD rats. The formulation exhibited a sol-gel transition at 33.5 °C within 17 s, with 40.6 ± 1.97% cumulative nasal permeation over 8 h. Medium-dose MFCH-TGL markedly reduced OVA-specific IgE (8.28 ± 1.64, P < 0.01) compared with the allergic model group (12.55 ± 1.86). Moreover, the gel displayed 1.46-fold longer half-life and 1.52-fold longer mean residence time than the MFCH aqueous solution. This thermosensitive in situ gel presents promising intranasal application potential, offering a feasible formulation strategy for traditional Chinese medicine against allergic rhinitis.
papers.title_ko: 알레르기 비염을 위한 목련화·구충초 열감응성 비강 내 제자리 겔: 제제화, 특성평가 및 생체 내 약동·약력 연구

summary.question: 목련화와 구충초 추출물을 담은 열감응성 비강 내 제자리 겔이 알레르기 비염에서 지속적 비강 전달과 항알레르기 효과를 높일 수 있는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: Poloxamer 기반 열감응성 겔(MFCH-TGL)을 제조한 뒤 물성·방출·비강 투과를 평가하고, BALB/c 생쥐와 SD 랫드에서 항알레르기 약력학과 비강 약동학을 조사했다.
summary.results: MFCH-TGL은 33.5°C에서 17초 내 겔화했으며, 중간용량에서 OVA 특이 IgE를 유의하게 낮추고, 수용액보다 반감기와 평균체류시간을 각각 1.46배와 1.52배 늘렸다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 비강 체류시간을 늘리기 위한 한약 비강 제형 전략으로서 가능성이 보이지만, 동물실험 결과이므로 임상 적용 해석에는 주의가 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 생체 내 결과가 동물모델에 국한되어 있어 사람 알레르기 비염에서의 유효성과 안전성은 명확한 정보 없음.

papers.title: Antioxidant and antiproliferative effects of flavonoid fractions from Citri Exocarpium Rubrum on A549 lung cancer cells and their underlying mechanisms by network pharmacology.
papers.journal: Natural product research
papers.authors: Wang J, Zeng S, Lu H, Chen Y, Wei M, Zeng G
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, with chemotherapy resistance limiting treatment efficacy. Citri Exocarpium Rubrum (CER), a flavonoid-rich traditional Chinese medicine, exhibits anticancer potential. This study investigated its antioxidant and antiproliferative effects against A549 lung cancer cells and the underlying mechanisms. Flavonoids were extracted from CER and partitioned into ethyl acetate and n-butanol fractions. Antioxidant capacity and antiproliferative effects were assessed by 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical and 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assays, respectively. Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and apoptosis were measured. Network pharmacology was conducted using TCMSP, SwissTargetPrediction and GeneCards, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Both fractions showed concentration-dependent DPPH radical scavenging (73.66% and 84.36% at 32 μg/mL) and inhibited A549 proliferation. The n-butanol fraction induced dose-dependent apoptosis with reduced MMP. Network pharmacology identified 6 active components, 255 targets, 5 hub targets (SRC, ESR1, BCL2, HSP90AA1, PPARG) and 20 enriched pathways related to cancer and calcium signalling. CER flavonoid fractions demonstrate antioxidant and antiproliferative activities against A549 cells via multi-component, multi-target mechanisms, supporting its potential clinical application in lung cancer therapy.

summary.question: 감귤류 과피 홍색부(CER) 플라보노이드 분획이 A549 폐암세포에서 항산화 및 항증식 효과를 보이는지와 그 기전을 확인하고자 했다.
summary.methods: CER 플라보노이드를 추출해 에틸아세테이트 및 n-부탄올 분획으로 나눈 뒤 DPPH, MTT, 미토콘드리아 막전위와 apoptosis를 평가하고 네트워크 약리학과 GO/KEGG 분석을 수행했다.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 본 연구는 CER 플라보노이드가 다성분·다표적 방식으로 폐암세포에 작용할 가능성을 시사하지만, 세포실험 결과이므로 임상 적용 가능성은 추가 검증이 필요하다.

papers.title: Non-pharmacological fatigue management strategies in neurodegenerative conditions: a scoping review.
papers.journal: Neurodegenerative disease management
papers.authors: Alageel S, Hibberd J, Deane KHO
papers.abstract:
Fatigue is a common and disabling symptom across several neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease. Non-pharmacological strategies are widely used in clinical practice to address fatigue, yet the extent to which evidence from one neurodegenerative condition can inform fatigue management in others remains uncertain, particularly for Parkinson's disease where intervention trials are scarce.
To map the quantitative evidence on non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults with neurodegenerative diseases (excluding dementias), and to identify potentially transferable strategies, gaps, and priorities for research and practice, with particular relevance to Parkinson's disease.
Scoping review conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported using the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/MJEYP).
MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, AMED, and PsycINFO were searched for records published from January 2006 to 15 February 2025. Reference lists of relevant reviews and included studies were screened. Publications in English or Arabic were eligible.
Quantitative interventional studies, mixed-methods studies with extractable quantitative fatigue outcomes, and systematic reviews/meta-analyses evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults with progressive neurodegenerative conditions were eligible. Conditions of interest included multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, motor neurone disease, Huntington's disease, hereditary ataxias, multiple system atrophy, and progressive supranuclear palsy. Studies focusing solely on pharmacological, surgical, herbal, or homeopathic interventions, qualitative-only studies, and studies in dementias were excluded.
A bespoke charting form captured study design, population, intervention, comparator, delivery format, fatigue measures, and key findings. Studies were grouped by intervention type: exercise, psychological, educational, and complementary interventions. Systematic reviews/meta-analyses and primary intervention studies were synthesized as distinct evidence levels and were not combined quantitatively.
The search identified 12,618 records. After removal of 5,399 duplicates, 7,219 records were screened and 517 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility. Twenty-seven sources met the inclusion criteria: seven systematic reviews/meta-analyses, 16 randomized controlled trials, one non-randomized controlled study, and three uncontrolled pre-post studies. Evidence was dominated by multiple sclerosis, with only two small trials in Parkinson's disease and no fatigue-focused intervention trials in other progressive neurodegenerative conditions. The most consistent between-group benefits were observed for structured exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and educational/self-management programs in multiple sclerosis. Complementary interventions included acupuncture, light therapy, dietary interventions, and electrical stimulation; evidence across these approaches was mixed. Heterogeneity in intervention type, intensity, duration, supervision and delivery format, follow-up duration, and fatigue outcome measures limited direct comparison across studies.
Non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in neurodegenerative disease are most developed in multiple sclerosis, where structured exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and educational/self-management approaches show the most consistent benefit. Evidence for Parkinson's disease is sparse, and no fatigue-focused intervention trials were identified in other progressive neurodegenerative conditions. Future work should prioritize condition-specific feasibility and effectiveness studies, harmonized fatigue outcome sets, objective fatigability measures alongside patient-reported fatigue, and multimodal programs with clearly specified therapeutic targets.

summary.question: 진행성 신경퇴행성 질환에서 비약물적 중재가 피로에 얼마나 유용한지와 다른 질환으로의 전이 가능성을 확인하고자 했다.
summary.methods: 2006년부터 2025년까지의 문헌을 대상으로 JBI 지침에 따라 수행한 범위 문헌고찰로, 정량적 중재연구와 체계적 문헌고찰을 포함해 피로 중재 근거를 유형별로 정리했다.
summary.results: 근거는 다발성경화증에 가장 많았고, 구조화된 운동·인지행동치료·교육/자가관리 중재가 가장 일관된 이점을 보였으며 파킨슨병 근거는 매우 제한적이었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 비약물적 피로 중재는 다발성경화증에서 가장 근거가 축적되어 있으나, 파킨슨병과 다른 신경퇴행성 질환에는 그대로 일반화하기 어렵다.

papers.title: Acupoint Thread Embedding for Weight Loss in Women With Overweight or Obesity : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: Annals of internal medicine
papers.authors: Xu S, Yang G, Hu C, Li X, Yin X, Zhao Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Whether acupoint thread embedding (ATE), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention, produces weight reduction remains uncertain.
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ATE for weight reduction in women with overweight or obesity.
Randomized, sham-controlled trial masked to participants, outcome assessors, and analysts. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06316310).
Acupuncture Department, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.
132 women aged 18 to 45 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24.0 kg/m2 or greater.
Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to ATE (6 sessions over 12 weeks) or sham ATE (superficial needle insertion at the same acupoints without manipulation, de qi, thread placement, or needle retention), followed by a 12-week follow-up.
The primary outcome was change in BMI from baseline to week 12, analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects models.
At week 12, BMI and body weight decreased 0.7 kg/m2 (95% CI, -1.0 to -0.3 kg/m2) and 1.8 kg (CI, -2.7 to -0.9 kg), respectively, more with ATE than with sham ATE; at week 24, differences were -1.1 kg/m2 (CI, -1.7 to -0.6 kg/m2) and -3.0 kg (CI, -4.5 to -1.6 kg), respectively. Weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 25.8% versus 9.1% (risk difference, 16.7 percentage points [CI, 3.7 to 29.3 percentage points]) at 12 weeks. Acupoint thread embedding produced greater reductions in waist and hip circumference, body fat percentage, and appetite scores, whereas cardiometabolic and patient-reported outcomes did not differ. Adverse events were mild and comparably distributed.
Single center, generally healthy women of reproductive age, unmasked acupuncturists, short-term follow-up, and underpowered for uncommon adverse events and subgroup analyses.
Acupoint thread embedding produced modest but sustained reductions in BMI and adiposity-related measures in Chinese women of reproductive age with overweight or obesity.
National Facility for Translational Medicine (Shanghai).

summary.results: 12주와 24주에 경혈 실 매입군이 가짜 시술군보다 BMI와 체중이 더 많이 감소했고, 허리·엉덩이둘레와 체지방률도 더 줄었으며 이상반응은 경미했다.

papers.title: Targeting the pyroptosis network: Research progress of natural products in intervention for acute lung injury.
papers.journal: British journal of pharmacology
papers.authors: Luo C, Tan J, Ning B, Ye Y, Tang Q, Jiang Z et al.
papers.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a serious clinical condition with high morbidity and mortality rates. Current ALI treatments have limitations. Natural products from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exhibit multi-component, multi-target and multi-pathway regulatory properties with good safety, making them promising candidates for ALI treatment. This review systematically summarizes the activation pathways of pyroptosis, its molecular regulatory network in ALI and the mechanisms by which natural products regulate pyroptosis to inhibit ALI progression. A 'natural products-pyroptosis-ALI' axis conceptual framework is proposed to provide theoretical support for clinical translation. Systematic literature searches were conducted on CNKI, Web of Science and PubMed up to March 2026, using keywords related to natural products, ALI and pyroptosis. This review covers TCM herbs, natural small-molecule compounds and TCM formulas that modulate pyroptosis to alleviate ALI, with all animal experiments adhering to ethical and international standards. Various natural products and TCM formulae effectively target pyroptosis, inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, Caspase-1 activation and Gasdermin D pore formation, thereby reducing IL-1β/IL-18 release, alleviating inflammatory cascades, protecting alveolar-capillary barrier integrity and mitigating oxidative stress. Activated pyroptosis further disturbs mitophagy, triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, engages the gut-lung axis, modulates epigenetic reprogramming and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition to amplify ALI. This review fills gaps in the systematic characterization of pyroptosis-ALI relationships and natural product-based therapies, aiming to expand ALI treatment options and advance ALI therapeutic development.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes of Thunder-fire moxibustion with or without Yiqi Wenyang Tincture for cancer-related fatigue: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Liu P, Du X, Li H, Zhao J, Zhong Y, Peng Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a debilitating symptom with limited treatment options. This study evaluated whether thunder-fire moxibustion (TFM) combined with Yiqi Wenyang Tincture (YWT) could provide additional benefit for CRF beyond conventional integrative management (control).
In a three-arm randomized controlled trial, 255 cancer patients were allocated (85 per group) to TFM alone, TFM plus YWT (TFM + YWT), or conventional integrative management (control). The primary outcomes were the Revised Piper Fatigue Scale (PFS-R) total score and EORTC QLQ-C30 global quality-of-life score at week 6.
In conservative intention-to-treat analyses using baseline observation carried forward for five missing week-6 assessments, with ANCOVA adjusted for baseline score and HC3 robust standard errors, TFM + YWT had lower PFS-R scores than TFM alone (adjusted mean difference, -0.459; 95% CI, -0.793 to -0.126; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.021) and higher global quality of life (2.552; 0.589 to 4.515; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.033). Exploratory outcomes were analyzed in the complete-case set.
TFM, particularly when combined with YWT, may provide incremental clinical benefit for CRF; confirmation in larger trials with matched attention controls and longer follow-up is warranted. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2200063288, and International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR), ChiMCTR2200006558; registered on September 3, 2022.

papers.title: Huanglian Jiedu Decoction: An Ethnopharmacological Perspective on Molecular Mechanisms and Clinical Applications in Inflammatory Diseases.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Li G, Liu Y, Li Q, Yang K, Wang Z, Wang L et al.
papers.abstract:
Huanglian Jiedu Decoction (HLJDD) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) renowned for its heat-clearing and detoxifying effects. For centuries, this formula has been widely used under the guidance of TCM theory to treat various inflammatory disorders characterized as "heat toxin" or "excess fire in the three burners." TCM considers "heat toxin" to be a common pathological mechanism underlying many inflammatory diseases, with clinical manifestations functionally analogous and corresponding to the infectious and non-infectious inflammation defined by modern Western medicine, rather than being strictly equivalent. Therefore, the traditional effects of HLJDD in clearing heat, purging fire, detoxifying, and cooling the blood provide a unique TCM theoretical foundation and alternative intervention strategy for the treatment of modern inflammatory diseases.
This review aims to systematically summarize the components, traditional efficacy, main active ingredients of HLJDD in inflammatory diseases, as well as its modern pharmacological effects and molecular mechanisms. By integrating traditional experience with modern scientific evidence, we strive to provide a solid scientific basis and translational strategies for the ethnomedicinal applications of this herbal medicine and its modern use in the prevention and treatment of inflammatory diseases.
A narrative literature search was performed in PubMed and CNKI from database inception to December 31, 2025, using "Huanglian Jiedu Decoction", "HLJDD", "anti-inflammatory", "inflammation" and their synonyms. Original research articles on the phytochemistry, network pharmacology, mechanisms, or clinical applications of HLJDD or its constituent herbs in inflammatory diseases were included; reviews, case reports, non-English/Chinese publications, and duplicates were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts, with disagreements resolved by consensus. A three-tier evidence classification (whole formula / single herb / pure compound) was applied to mechanistic studies, and findings were synthesized narratively given substantial heterogeneity. Only PubMed and CNKI were searched, which may limit comprehensiveness.
The anti-inflammatory activity of HLJDD is mainly attributed to its various alkaloids and flavonoid compounds. These components exert synergistic effects through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms, significantly inhibiting the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and effectively regulating the activation of key inflammatory signaling pathways (such as NF-κB, MAPK, JAK-STAT, and the NLRP3 inflammasome). Both in vivo and in vitro experiments have confirmed that HLJDD exhibits significant anti-inflammatory and tissue-protective effects in various inflammatory disease models, including sepsis, acute lung injury, colitis, and skin inflammation. Its mechanism of action is characterized by a typical "multi-component, multi-target, multi-pathway" network regulation feature.
What is established is that HLJDD and its constituent compounds modulate the NF-κB, MAPK, JAK-STAT, and NLRP3 pathways in cellular and animal systems, although most mechanistic evidence derives from isolated compounds rather than the whole formula. What is suggestive is that HLJDD-containing interventions may confer clinical benefit in selected inflammatory conditions; however, current clinical evidence remains of very low certainty, as most reported studies are small-sample, non-blinded trials using modified formulas or combination therapies rather than the classic HLJDD formula alone. What remains hypothetical is whether these preclinical mechanisms translate into clinically meaningful efficacy in humans. Future research should therefore prioritize: in-depth mechanistic studies that rigorously distinguish whole-formula from compound-level evidence; standardized extraction and quality-control systems; delivery systems to improve bioavailability; and large-scale, rigorously designed randomized controlled trials-so that HLJDD may progressively advance from empirical use toward a safe and effective evidence-based anti-inflammatory therapy..

papers.title: Acupuncture alleviates post-stroke depression by inhibiting proline-driven ferroptosis in hippocampal neurons.
papers.journal: Neuroscience
papers.authors: Sun P, Zou L, Li N, Liu H, Sun M, Xie J et al.
papers.abstract:
Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a prevalent stroke complication with scarce therapeutic interventions. Acupuncture has shown clinical efficacy in PSD, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates whether acupuncture alleviates PSD by regulating proline metabolism-mediated ferroptosis.
We generated a rat PSD model via common carotid artery ligation coupled with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Acupuncture at GV20, GV26, GV24, and GV14 was administered for four weeks. Behavioral tests, TTC and Nissl staining, ELISA, qPCR, western blot, amino acid metabolomics, and hippocampal neuron cultures with proline intervention were performed.
Acupuncture robustly rescued depression-like phenotypes and mitigated hippocampal neuronal injury in PSD rats. Acupuncture decreased serum levels of iron ions, malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), increased glutathione (GSH), and reversed the aberrant expression of ferroptosis-related proteins (GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4, TFR1) in the hippocampus. Amino acid metabolomics revealed elevated serum proline in PSD rats, which was normalized by acupuncture. Exogenous proline administration aggravated depressive behaviors and hippocampal ferroptosis. In cultured hippocampal neurons, high-dose proline directly induced ferroptosis and reduced cell viability.
Acupuncture ameliorates PSD by inhibiting hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis through regulation of proline metabolism, revealing a novel mechanism for acupuncture treatment.

papers.title: Acupuncture versus conventional therapy for painful temporomandibular disorders in women: a study protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.authors: Citó EBC, Coutinho BD, de Moraes MEA, Vale ML, Gondim DV
papers.abstract:
The prevalence of temporomandibular disorder (TMD) has been increasing, and its high rate of chronicity makes it a relevant public health concern. Despite the availability of several treatment options, there is still no consensus regarding the most effective approach for managing painful TMD.
This study presents the protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness of acupuncture compared with conventional treatment in patients with painful TMD.
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) systemic individualized acupuncture based on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis; (2) local acupuncture according to Western diagnostic criteria; or (3) standard treatment consisting of oral splint therapy and pharmacotherapy. TMD will be assessed using the DC/TMD Axis I protocol. Evaluations will be performed at baseline, after the intervention period, and at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. All treatment protocols will last eight weeks. The primary outcome is pain intensity, assessed by the Numeric Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes include pain interference in daily life, jaw functional limitation, oral behaviors, anxiety, depression, and somatization (DC/TMD Axis II instruments). Sleep quality will be evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and salivary cortisol levels will serve as an exploratory physiological biomarker associated with stress response.
Data collection and analysis are ongoing; results will determine comparative treatment efficacy across all groups.
This is the first clinical trial to compare individualized acupuncture based on TCM with a standardized acupuncture protocol derived from Western diagnosis in the management of painful TMD. The findings are expected to contribute to evidence-based clinical practice and improve therapeutic decision-making for this complex condition.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture combined with traditional Chinese medicine therapy improves non-alcoholic steatohepatitis by regulating the TLR4/NF-κB and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways.
papers.journal: Pathology, research and practice
papers.authors: Mi L, Chen J, Li J, Gao F, Wang L, Dong Q et al.
papers.abstract: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), an advanced stage of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), is characterized by hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress, yet effective pharmacological therapies remain limited. The present study investigated the therapeutic effects and potential underlying mechanisms of electroacupuncture (EA) combined with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction in a high-fat diet-induced rat model of NASH. Rats were treated with EA, TCM decoction, or their combination, and liver pathology, biochemical parameters, transcriptomic profiles, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and related signaling pathways were comprehensively evaluated. Combined EA and TCM treatment markedly reduced liver weight and liver index, alleviated hepatic steatosis and histopathological injury, improved liver function by decreasing serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels, and ameliorated lipid and glucose metabolism disorders. Transcriptome sequencing identified 351 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment analyses indicating that inflammatory and oxidative stress-related pathways were potentially associated with the interventional effect. Molecular results showed that the combined treatment significantly suppressed the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway, resulting in decreased the expression of inflammatory mediators, and simultaneously activated the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway to enhance cellular antioxidant defense. In addition, HSD11B1 expression was markedly downregulated, suggesting its potential involvement in mediating the interplay between lipid metabolism and inflammatory responses during disease progression. Overall, in this high-fat diet-induced rat NASH model, EA combined with TCM decoction ameliorates NASH-related pathological alterations by regulating the TLR4/NF-κB and Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathways, improving hepatic pathology, restoring metabolic homeostasis, suppressing inflammation, and attenuating oxidative stress damage. This combined intervention regimen provides preclinical evidence for future studies on NASH therapy.

papers.title: [Development of an optimal acupuncture-moxibustion treatment protocol for perimenopausal insomnia].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Tian L, Wang Z, Chen Q, Li J, Yang X, Han J
papers.abstract:
To systematically evaluate various acupuncture-moxibustion treatment regimens for perimenopausal insomnia using network meta-analysis combined with multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) approach, and to identify interventions with optimal overall efficacy across multiple dimensions, so as to provide a scientific basis for clinical decision-making.
Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on acupuncture-moxibustion treatment for perimenopausal insomnia published from database inception to September 27, 2025 were systematically searched in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Chinese Journal Service Platform (VIP), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform, China Biology Medicine Database (SinoMed), PubMed, EMbase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science. Network meta-analysis was performed using R software (version 4.4.3), and surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) value was calculated. A multidimensional evaluation system was established using the total effective rate, Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI) score, and modified Kupperman menopausal index (KMI) score as efficacy indexes, and treatment frequency as the cost index. The entropy weight method was applied to determine index weight, and the weighted normalized decision matrix was analyzed using technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) and multi-criteria optimization and compromise solution (Vlsekriterijumska Optimizacija I Kompromisno Resenje, VIKOR), two methods of MCDM, to comprehensively rank different acupuncture-moxibustion related interventions.
A total of 32 RCTs were finally eligible, involving 19 acupuncture-moxibustion related protocols and 3 control measures. Network meta-analysis showed: for the total effective rate, the cumulative ranking curve was high for depression-relieving acupuncture therapy combined with western medication (SUCRA = 0.76), mind-regulating acupuncture therapy combined with Chinese herbal medication (SUCRA=0.75), and acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle (SUCRA=0.75); for improvement in PSQI scores, cumulative ranking curve was high for abdominal acupuncture combined with Chinese herbal medication (SUCRA=0.93), depression-relieving acupuncture therapy combined with western medication (SUCRA=0.93), and acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle (SUCRA= 0.84); and for improvement in modified KMI scores, it was high for warm needling (SUCRA=0.95), time-based acupoint selection acupuncture (SUCRA=0.79), and scalp acupuncture (SUCRA=0.76). MCDM analysis on treatment frequency demonstrated that acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle ranked first in both TOPSIS and VIKOR methods, with relative closeness of 0.780 8 and Q value of 0, respectively.
Acupuncture at back-shu points of five zang organs combined with warming needle demonstrates the advantages in both efficacy and cost, showing superior comprehensive performance among various acupuncture-moxibustion related interventions for perimenopausal insomnia, and it may serve as a clinically recommended option.

papers.title: [Compilation of extraordinary points based on 1963 edition of Illustrated Handbook of Extraordinary Points in Acupuncture and Moxibustion].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xu R, Zhuang R, Wu J, Li B
papers.abstract: This paper systematically investigates the compilation of the 1963 edition of Illustrated Handbook of Extraordinary Points in Acupuncture and Moxibustion through literature traceability and textual comparison study. This book has made significant contributions to the collection of literature on extraordinary points and content verification. However, some literature citations exhibited issues such as failing to trace the original sources, copying error on main indications of treatment, or bibliographic information misrepresentation; and there was a certain disconnect between the extensive compilation of literature and its subsequent processing. Hence, the paper explores how the compilation experience of Illustrated Handbook of Extraordinary Points in Acupuncture and Moxibustion can provide insights for contemporary research on the systematization of extraordinary points, and suggests enhancing the rigor and transparency of literature traceability and effectively utilizing digital tools to support research.

papers.title: [Return to a people-centered, individualized acupuncture diagnosis and treatment system].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Yu C, Niu Q, Liang S, Zhang L, Sun Y
papers.abstract: This article presents a review and commentary on technical generalization commonly existing in contemporary clinical acupuncture-moxibustion practice. The study highlights that clinical malpractice, "treating superficial or minor ailments using robust needle techniques (large needle)", not only leads to serious adverse outcomes including tissue damage and excessive depletion of qi and blood, but also deviates from the essential theories of TCM, which emphasizes the harmonization of yin and yang, and a patient-centered approach. By analyzing the current lack of the theory of "nine ancient needles", "each needle performs its specific function" in modern clinical practice, this study explores the underlying causes of this phenomenon from multiple dimensions including economic benefits, educational system, and research orientation; and proposes a solution for establishing an individualized treatment framework across three dimensions: reform in clinical practice, reconstruction of the teaching framework, and innovation in research standards. This paper emphasizes that only by returning to the classical concept of acupuncture and moxibustion, "comprehensive integrated treatment" and establishing a diagnostic and therapeutic evaluation system tailored to the characteristics of acupuncture and moxibustion, can the discipline of acupuncture and moxibustion achieve sustainable development and provide higher-quality healthcare services for human health.

papers.title: [Examination of folk acupuncture-moxibustion practice in the Song Dynasty based on Jiu Ai Tu].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang L
papers.abstract: As the earliest extant pictorial artwork depicting acupuncture-moxibustion-related medical customs, Jiu Ai Tu (Illustrations of Moxibustion and Acupuncture) provides invaluable visual historical materials for the study of the folk healthcare ecosystem during the Song Dynasty. From the perspective of medical iconography, the paper introduces a systematic interpretation of the physician-patient relationship, perceptions of disease, and therapeutic techniques of acupuncture and moxibustion depicted in this painting. By examining the identities of practitioners of traditional Chinese medicine, patient conditions, and various therapeutic approaches, including direct moxibustion with multiple cones, acupuncture for pus drainage, and external application of medicated plasters, this study reveals the interactive relationship between folk acupuncture practice during the Song Dynasty and the records preserved in medical texts. Furthermore, from a social historical standpoint, it explores the medical ecosystem of physician-patient relationship in the folk, the divergent fates of acupuncture-moxibustion therapies across different social strata, and the influence of the public dissemination of medical knowledge during the Song Dynasty, thereby providing a perspective from social history of knowledge for understanding the diverse dimensions of the medical society during the Song Dynasty.

papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Lian Y
papers.abstract: Although the theory of guimen thirteen needles is widely disseminated, its diverse origins and complex development have led to numerous opinions and interpretations. This article reviews the controversies regarding this theory across different historical periods and medical schools, and critically examines the views proposed by Bian Que, Ge Hong, Zhang Zhenren before the Tang Dynasty, as well as those put forward by Sun Zhenren and Xu Qiufu after the Tang Dynasty, so as to clarify the academic context and historical background of the theory of guimen thirteen needles, thereby refining the research on the origins of various interpretations of it. Furthermore, it is necessary to note the key cultural contexts associated and preserved in folk traditions regarding the various interpretations of the theory of guimen thirteen needles.

papers.title: [Wentong Kangyan theory: interpretation and construction of theoretical model of moxibustion effect based on chronic vascular inflammation].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xu Q, Zhang T, Song X, Wang H, Hu X, Gao S et al.
papers.abstract: The paper addresses the explanatory predicament regarding the lack of logical coherence between the theory of moxibustion for warming and unblocking blood vessels and the pathology of chronic vascular inflammation, a theoretical model of Wentong Kangyan (warming and unblocking blood vessels for anti-inflammation) was constructed by systematically integrating biological evidence. This model elucidates the effect of moxibustion as a sequential biological process. Using surface thermal stimulation as a physical activation signal (promoting blood circulation by warming action of moxibustion), moxibustion activates the neuro-immune-vascular network to achieve systemic inflammatory homeostatic remodeling (anti-inflammation by warming and unblocking action) and specifically mediates improvement in vascular endothelial function (unblocking blood vessel and promoting blood circulation). This structured pathway, "body surface activation- systemic regulation-targeting effect", not only provides a logically consistent interpretation of classical theory based on modern science, but also demonstrates the construction pathway for transforming traditional acupuncture-moxibustion wisdom into verifiable theoretical model, representing a conscious practice to advance acupuncture-moxibustion research from empirical description towards theoretical formalization.

papers.title: [Approach of the "three-adjustment" acupuncture and moxibustion to autonomic nervous system dysfunction based on the "regulating brain-mind, regulating heart-mind, and regulating spleen- stomach"].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Shen T, Xiao Z, Li Y, Yu X, Wang Z
papers.abstract: Autonomic nervous system dysfunction (ANSD) primarily manifests as symptoms such as insomnia, tinnitus, palpitations, chest tightness, and dyspepsia. Acupuncture and moxibustion exert the effects of unblocking meridians and harmonizing yin and yang, and hold unique advantages and clinical value in treatment of ANSD. Based on its common clinical manifestations and TCM theory regarding zangfu organs, it is viewed that the core pathogenesis of ANSD is characterized by "impairment of brain-mind in coordination, heart-mind disturbance, and dysfunction of spleen and stomach". Based on this, "three-adjustment" acupuncture and moxibustion, "regulating brain-mind, regulating heart-mind, and regulating spleen-stomach", is proposed as the general therapeutic principle for "mind adjustment", taking both form and mind into consideration and treating both root and branch. Clinically, Baihui (GV20) and Fengchi (GB20) are used to regulate the brain-mind; Neiguan (PC6) and Shenmen (HT7) are used to regulate the heart-mind; Zusanli (ST36) and Shangjuxu (ST37) are to regulate the spleen and stomach. Mind is primarily regulated prior to the body, and deqi and gentle stimulation are required specifically. Modern studies suggest that the three groups of core acupoints are involved in the regulation of autonomic nervous function through central nervous system, cardiac autonomic nervous system, and vagus nerve, providing a solid foundation of modern research for the clinical application of "three-adjustment" method of acupuncture and moxibustion. Such therapy adopts an integrated approach to "brain-heart-spleen-stomach" system, centers at "mind adjustment", and offers a novel perspective for treatment of ANSD with acupuncture and moxibustion.

papers.title: [ZHUANG Lixing's clinical experience for sudden hearing loss with the "regulating the spirit and restoring the pivot" acupuncture method].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Han M, Liao K, Zhan J, Zeng Y, Zhuang L
papers.abstract: This article summarizes Professor ZHUANG Lixing 's clinical experience for sudden hearing loss with the "regulating the spirit and restoring the pivot" acupuncture method. Professor ZHUANG considers that the disease is mostly caused by emotional disturbance and dysfunction of the Shaoyang pivot, and advocates early acupuncture and moxibustion intervention. The pathogenesis of "closure of the orifices and concealment of the spirit as the manifestation, and impaired pivot mechanism as the root" should be closely followed, and the therapeutic principle of "regulating the spirit as the priority and restoring the pivot as the key" should be applied. In clinical practice, acupoints on the governor vessel, such as Shenting (GV24) and Yintang (GV24+), are selected to regulate the spirit, while acupoints on the Shaoyang meridians, such as Tinghui (GB2) and Yifeng (TE17), are selected to restore the pivot, supplemented by flexible selection of additional acupoints according to the presenting pattern. Together, these methods open the orifices and relieve obstruction, unblock the ear, and restore hearing.

papers.title: [YANG Jun's clinical experience in treating rotational spasmodic torticollis through differentiation on pathogenesis, sinews/fascia of meridians and muscles].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhang J, Xiao H, Zhang Q, Cui J, Huang Z, Zhang L et al.
papers.abstract: The paper introduces Professor YANG Jun 's clinical experience in diagnosis and treatment of rotational spasmodic torticollis with acupuncture and moxibustion. Professor YANG believes that this disorder is rooted in yang deficiency, manifesting clinically as disturbances caused by internal and external wind pathogens. The crucial factor lies on the impaired distribution of the governor vessel, and the location of disorder is on sinews/fascia of meridians. Under the general principle of "yang deficiency with wind agitation", it is essential to precisely differentiate three syndromes/patterns, including cold-dampness obstructing the collaterals, yin deficiency stirring up wind, and phlegm-stasis obstructing the collaterals. The treatment approach focuses on regulating yang and unblocking the governor vessel, as well as relaxing tendons and relieving spasms; and it emphasizes a layered therapeutic strategy based on three distinct levels, i.e., identifying the underlying pathogenic mechanism, assessing the affected sinews/fascia of meridians, and determining the targeted muscle groups. Differentiating pathogenesis is to distinguish the deficiency of root causes from the excess of clinical symptoms, differentiating sinews/fascia of meridians is to determine the location of illness, and differentiating muscles serves to identify the affected muscle groups. In treatment, the local acupoints are selected precisely and combined with the distal ones based on meridian distribution, the appropriate acupoints are used in accordance with the specific syndromes/patterns, the acupoints of the governor vessel are especially combined with scalp acupuncture. In operation, transverse needling, point-toward-point needling, surrounding needling and bone-targeting needle techniques are employed. All the aforementioned provide the references for clinical diagnosis and treatment of rotational spasmodic torticollis.

papers.title: [WANG Jihong's experience in treatment of thyroid nodules with Tongyuan acupuncture therapy and "five acupoints from tianyou"].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Huang S, Li Z, Huang Z, Li H, Wang J, Hou J
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Professor WANG Jihong's clinical experience in treatment of thyroid nodules with Tongyuan acupuncture therapy and "five acupoints from tianyou". Based on the theoretical framework of "mind/spirit, qi, the origin and body", as well as the holistic idea of TCM such as "nourishing mind/spirit" and "guiding qi ", thyroid nodules are treated in stages. In the early stage, the acupoints for unblocking the governor vessel and nourishing mind/spirit are selected, including Baihui (GV20), Yintang (CV24+), Dazhui (GV14), and Zhiyang (GV9). In the later stage, the acupoints for guiding qi back to the origin are selected, such as Guanyuan (CV4), Qihai (CV6), Danzhong (CV17), and Tianshu (ST25). Throughout the entire course of treatment, Renying (ST9) and Futu (LI18), two of the key points from "five acupoints from tianyou" documented in the Huangdi Neijing (Yellow Emperor 's Inner Classic) are incorporated to regulate qi movement and resolve tangible pathogenic accumulations in the neck region. This distinctive therapeutic approach embodies the principles of "addressing both symptoms and root cause simultaneously" and "mutual regulation of body and qi " in treatment. It not only alleviates the symptoms of thyroid nodules but also restores the dynamic equilibrium of "mind/spirit, qi, the origin and body", so as to reduce local lesion size, and the risk of malignant transformation, thereby obtaining the specific therapeutic effect of TCM, "prevention before disease onset, and prevention of progression after onset".

papers.title: [Acupuncture for facial laxity and sagging based on SHI Xuemin's meridian sinew acupuncture method].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Li M, Peng T, Guo Y
papers.abstract: Based on Academician SHI Xuemin's meridian sinew acupuncture method, this article proposes the "four facial lifting methods" for the treatment of facial laxity and sagging, using facial acupuncture, stuck needle manipulation, acupotomy, and filiform needle acupuncture. Facial acupuncture, stuck needle manipulation, and acupotomy stimulate the meridian sinews to improve the "longitudinal sinews" of the hand and foot yang meridians in the facial and cervical regions. Filiform needle acupuncture with reinforcing methods could regulate qi and blood, promoting the upward nourishment of qi and blood to face. By utilizing the advantages of different acupuncture techniques to stimulate the meridian sinew system, this method treats both the root and the manifestations, achieving facial lifting effects and promoting facial rejuvenation, and provides a new approach for acupuncture cosmetology.

papers.title: [Effects of electroacupuncture on epididymal function and sperm quality in obese rats based on mitochondrial apoptosis pathway].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhang J, Xiao Y, Li G, Yuan R, Huang X, Shen Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of electroacupuncture (EA) on epididymal function and sperm quality in obese rats, and explore the molecular mechanisms underlying EA-mediated improvement in obesity-related reproductive dysfunction.
Of 40 male Wistar rats, 8 rats were randomized as a blank group, and the rest rats were fed with high-fat diet for 8 weeks to establish obesity models. Twenty-four successfully modeled rats were randomly allocated into amodel group (n=8), an EA group (n=8), and a dietary adjustment group (n=8). The rats in the EA group received EA at "Zusanli" (ST36) and "Sanyinjiao" (SP6) using dense-disperse waves at 2 Hz/15 Hz frequency and 1.5 mA intensity for 30 min per session, 5 sessions per week, for 4 consecutive weeks. In the dietary adjustment group, the rats were fed regularly for 4 weeks. After intervention completion, body weight, body mass index (BMI), and Lee's index were recorded. HE staining was used to examine the morphology and mass of epididymal tissue and epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT). Enzymatic colorimetric assay was employed to detect the levels of triglycerides (TG), total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) in serum. Computer-aided sperm analysis system was used to assess sperm motility and sperm concentration in rats, the sperm chromatin dispersion assay was used to determine the sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI), the dual-fluorescence staining combined with flow cytometry was used to assess the level of sperm apoptosis in the epididymis, the enzyme-linked spectrophotometry was used to quantitatively measure adenosine triphosphate (ATP) content in the epididymis, JC-1 fluorescence probe staining combined with flow cytometry was used to determine the mitochondrial membrane potential level in the epididymal cells; and Western blot was used to detect the protein expression levels of B-cell lymphoma-2 gene (BCL-2), BCL-2-associated X protein (BAX), Cytochrome c, cleaved cysteine-aspartate protease (Caspase)-3 and cleaved-Caspase-9 in the epididymis; the real-time quantitative PCR was used to detect the mRNA expression levels of BCL-2, BAX, Cytochrome c, Caspase-3 and Caspase-9 in the epididymis.
Compared with the blank group, the model group showed the increased body weight, BMI, and Lee's index (P<0.01), reduced relative epididymal mass (P<0.01); increased eWAT mass, relative eWAT mass, and mean eWAT adipocyte area (P<0.01); elevated serum TG, TC, and LDL-C levels (P<0.01), and decreased serum HDL-C level (P<0.01); disrupted epididymal tissue structure, reduced sperm concentration and motility (P<0.01), increased sperm DFI (P<0.01), and elevated sperm apoptosis rate (P<0.01); decreased epididymal mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP content (P<0.01); reduced protein and mRNA expression of BCL-2 (P<0.01), and increased protein expression of BAX, Cytochrome c, cleaved-Caspase-3 and cleaved-Caspase-9 (P<0.01), and the mRNA expression of BAX, Cytochrome c, Caspase-3 and Caspase-9. Compared with the model group, except for average adipocyte area, sperm concentration, sperm apoptosis rate, mitochondrial membrane potential, and BCL-2 protein expression, all other parameters in the EA group and the dietary adjustment group showed the improvements (P<0.01, P<0.05). Compared with the dietary adjustment group, the EA group exhibited the reduced body weight, average adipocyte area, serum TG, TC, and LDL-C levels, the protein and mRNA expression of Cytochrome c, as well as decreased mRNA expression of Caspase-3 and Caspase-9 (P<0.01, P<0.05); and the increases of the relative epididymal mass, sperm concentration and motility, serum HDL-C level, ATP content, and BCL-2 protein expression (P<0.01, P<0.05).
Electroacupuncture can effectively improve epididymal function and sperm quality in obese male rats, and the underlying mechanism may be associated with inhibiting the activation of the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway and maintaining mitochondrial functional homeostasis.

papers.title: [Mechanism research of Tongdu Tiaoshen acupuncture on post-stroke depression from the perspective of hippocampal neuron ferroptosis].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zou L, Zhang D, Yang S, Gao Z, Teng Z, Sun M et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of Tongdu Tiaoshen (unblocking the governor vessel and regulating the mind) acupuncture on post-stroke depression (PSD) from the perspective of hippocampal neuron ferroptosis, so as to explore the mechanism of this therapy on PSD.
Twenty-seven male SD rats were randomly divided into a sham-operation group (n=9) and a modeling group (n=18). PSD models were established by right unilateral common carotid artery occlusion combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) in the modeling group. The successfully modeled rats were randomly assigned to a model group (n=9) and a Tongdu Tiaoshen acupuncture group (n=9). In the Tongdu Tiaoshen group, Tongdu Tiaoshen acupuncture was delivered at "Baihui" (GV20), "Shenting" (GV24), "Shuigou" (GV26) and "Dazhui" (GV14), once daily, 6 interventions per week, with one day of rest, for a continuous intervention period of 4 weeks. The depression-like behaviors and neurofunctional impairment were assessed using open-field test, sucrose preference test, and the Zea Longa neurobehavioral score in rats. HE and Nissl staining were employed to observe neuronal morphology in the hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG region) of rats. ELISA was adopted to determine the levels of hippocampal iron ion, glutathione (GSH), malondialdehyde (MDA), and reactive oxygen species (ROS) in rats; and Western blot and real-time quantitative PCR were used to detect the protein and mRNA expression of hippocampal glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), transferrin receptor 1 (TFR1), solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11) in rats separately.
Compared with the sham-operation group, in the model group, the moving distance and stay time in the central area of the open-field test, as well as sucrose preference rate were reduced (P<0.05), and the Zea Longa neurobehavioral score increased (P<0.05); the morphology of neurons in the hippocampal DG region was abnormal, the matrix was relatively loose, and the number of neuronal death increased (P<0.05); the levels of iron ion, MDA and ROS rose (P<0.05), and the level of GSH was reduced (P<0.05); the protein and mRNA expression of GPX4 and SLC7A11 in hippocampus decreased (P<0.05), and that of ACSL4 and TFR1 increased (P<0.05). When compared with the model group, in the Tongdu Tiaoshen acupuncture group, the moving distance and stay time in the central area of the open-field test, as well as sucrose preference rate increased (P<0.05), and the Zea Longa neurobehavioral score was reduced (P<0.05); the morphology of neurons in hippocampal DG region was improved obviously, the matrix was relatively dense, and the number of neuronal death was declined (P<0.05); the levels of iron ion, MDA and ROS in hippocampus were reduced (P<0.05), and the content of GSH was elevated (P<0.05); the protein and mRNA expression of GPX4 and SLC7A11 in hippocampus increased (P<0.05), and that of ACSL4 and TFR1 decreased (P<0.05).
Tongdu Tiaoshen acupuncture can alleviate depression-like behaviors in PSD modeled rats, and its mechanism is related to the inhibition of ferroptosis in hippocampal neurons.

papers.title: [Analysis of constructing an evidence ecological approach for acupoint selection in acupuncture and moxibustion based on multi-source evidence].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Niu Q, Wang X, Yu C
papers.abstract: Addressing the evidence selection dilemma in acupoint selection in clinical practice of acupuncture and moxibustion, as well as the conflict between standardization and individualization, this study innovatively proposes the establishment of an evidence-based ecological approach to acupoint selection schemes grounded in multi-source evidence. By introducing the evidence challenges encountered in clinical acupuncture-moxibustion practice and the need for innovation in research paradigm, the paper systematically analyzes the connotation, characteristics and similarities/differences of multi-source evidence. It elaborates on the methodology for constructing the evidence ecological approach, comprising four steps, i.e., evidence mining and visual mapping, mechanism interpretation and logical integration, protocol generation and consensus decision-making, and dynamic validation and iterative optimization. Besides, a case study on knee osteoarthritis treatment is provided to demonstrate the approach. This study aims to establish a "core-module" based acupoint selection methodological pathway that integrates traditional classical text knowledge, expert experience, randomized controlled trial, data mining, and guidelines/expert consensus. By employing a dynamic validation for iterative optimization, this approach provides clinicians with a decision-support tool that combines standardized foundations with personalized flexibility, thereby driving the evolution of clinical practice of acupuncture and moxibustion toward a data-driven, evidence-integrated paradigm.

papers.title: [Effects of Acupuncture and Hand Therapy on Immune-Related Markers].
papers.journal: Gan to kagaku ryoho. Cancer & chemotherapy
papers.authors: Okochi T, Ikeda M, Yamada S, Nishikido O, Inoue Y, Sasaki A
papers.abstract: This study aimed to clarify the effects of acupuncture and hand therapy on physical and mental relaxation and immune function, by measuring changes in autonomic nervous system activity and salivary oxytocin and cortisol concentrations before and after acupuncture treatment. The results showed a significant decrease in sympathetic nervous activity and a trend toward increased parasympathetic nervous activity. Furthermore, oxytocin levels increased significantly, while cortisol levels decreased significantly. These physiological changes indicate that the treatments have a relaxing effect and may contribute to enhancing natural immune function. These results are significant from the perspective of maintaining a state of "pre-disease."

papers.title: Immediate Analgesic Effect of Acupuncture for Primary Dysmenorrhea: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of pain research
papers.authors: Zhang P, Li M, Lv J
papers.abstract:
This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the immediate analgesic effect of acupuncture for primary dysmenorrhea (PD), characterize its time-effect profile, and identify core influencing factors.
We systematically searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP databases from January 2006 to April 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating acupuncture for PD. Two reviewers independently performed study screening, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment (RoB 2.0). Meta-analyses used RevMan 5.4.1; evidence certainty was rated with GRADE.
Thirty-six RCTs with 3,532 PD patients were included. Compared with blank control, single-point acupuncture produced analgesia from 5 minutes post-insertion, peaked at 30 minutes (MD = -30.86, 95% CI: -39.91 to -21.81, P < 0.00001), and persisted to 120 minutes post-withdrawal. Single-point acupuncture outperformed non-acupoint shallow needling (MD = -9.96, 95% CI: -19.16 to -0.75, P = 0.03),Sanyinjiao (SP6) exhibited a more prominent analgesic effect trend compared with Xuanzhong (GB39). Multi-acupoint combination was superior to single-point acupuncture (MD = -3.70, 95% CI: -5.82 to -1.57, P = 0.0007), stronger Deqi outperformed weaker Deqi (MD = -7.54, 95% CI: -10.05 to -5.02, P < 0.00001). At 30 minutes, acupuncture had greater analgesic effect than conventional medication (SMD = -2.97, 95% CI: -4.45 to -1.49, P < 0.0001); however, this comparison had very high heterogeneity (I2 = 96%) and very low GRADE certainty, and trim-and-fill correction suggested possible overestimation due to publication bias.
Acupuncture provides rapid-onset immediate analgesia for PD, with acupoint specificity, multi-acupoint combination, and Deqi intensity as key effect modifiers. Given the very low to moderate certainty of evidence and high heterogeneity, these findings are preliminary and require confirmation through large-sample, standardized, multicenter RCTs.

papers.title: Gut-derived signals in type 2 diabetes-associated dry eye: current evidence, causal uncertainty, and validation priorities.
papers.journal: Frontiers in medicine
papers.authors: Wei Q, Ding N, Fan S, Liang S, Gan L, Wu Y
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)-associated dry eye disease (DED) includes aqueous, evaporative, epithelial, inflammatory, and neurosensory phenotypes. Intestinal dysbiosis may contribute to some of these abnormalities, but the clinical and mechanistic evidence has not yet been synthesised in terms of disease relevance and causal strength. We conducted a structured narrative review using iterative PubMed searches, full-text retrieval from PubMed Central and publisher websites, and backward citation tracing. The evidence pool was updated to 26 July 2026. Human studies in T2DM consistently report neuropathy, corneal sensory or nerve changes, meibomian dysfunction, and lacrimal injury, but no human study jointly measuring intestinal microbiota or gut-derived metabolites with T2DM-DED outcomes was found. One disease-matched animal study linked a probiotic-prebiotic intervention with changes in intestinal, lacrimal, inflammatory, and dry-eye-like features. Other experimental models support microbiota-sensitive lacrimal responses, macrophage-dependent corneal nerve repair, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-responsive ocular-surface homeostasis. Taken together, these findings establish model-specific effects rather than a continuous human pathway. SCFAs are therefore considered a hypothesis-prioritised candidate based on cross-model breadth, although their necessity, sufficiency, and mediation in T2DM-DED remain unknown. Diet, glycaemic control, obesity, renal function, neuropathy, medicines, and ocular treatment are important clinical confounders. Future studies should combine longitudinal human co-phenotyping with a disease-matched mediation experiment that measures intestinal, metabolic, lacrimal, corneal-neural, and ocular-surface outcomes in the same temporal sequence. Oral Chinese herbal medicine is presented only as one standardisable perturbation for such testing, rather than as an established gut-mediated therapy.

papers.title: Acupuncture before and during letrozole ovulation induction in women with overweight or obesity and PCOS-related infertility: a randomized sham-controlled pilot trial.
papers.journal: Frontiers in endocrinology
papers.authors: Dou Z, Zhang Y, Hao J, Zhao X, Zhu H, Gong Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Obesity-related metabolic dysfunction may impair fertility outcomes in women with overweight or obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). We evaluated acupuncture initiated 3 months before letrozole ovulation induction and continued during treatment.
In this single-center, randomized, participant-blinded, sham-controlled pilot trial, 60 women aged 20-35 years with a body mass index ≥25 kg/m² were assigned 1:1 to acupuncture or nonpenetrating sham acupuncture. Both groups received lifestyle guidance. Interventions were administered during the 3-month pretreatment phase and up to three letrozole cycles. The primary outcomes were continuing pregnancy and live birth. Secondary outcomes included other reproductive, anthropometric, metabolic, endometrial, and uterine artery Doppler outcomes.
A total of 60 women were randomized, 55 completed follow-up and were included in the per-protocol analysis, while all 60 were included in the intention-to-treat analyses of pregnancy outcomes. In the per-protocol analysis, the live-birth rate was significantly higher in the acupuncture group than in the sham acupuncture group (14/27 [51.9%] vs. 6/28 [21.4%]; P = 0.03). The continuing-pregnancy rates were 14/27 (51.9%) and 8/28 (28.6%), respectively (P = 0.10). The biochemical-pregnancy rate was also higher in the acupuncture group (17/27 [63.0%] vs. 9/28 [32.1%]; P = 0.03), whereas clinical pregnancy and pregnancy loss did not differ significantly between the groups. The intention-to-treat analyses showed similar effect directions, although the differences were not statistically significant for live birth (46.7% vs. 20.0%; P = 0.054) or continuing pregnancy (46.7% vs. 26.7%; P = 0.18). Cycle-level ovulation was summarized descriptively. Acupuncture was associated with greater improvements in body weight, glucose and lipid metabolism, insulin resistance, leptin, and adiponectin and with more favorable endometrial thickness and morphology and uterine artery Doppler indices (all P < 0.05). No serious adverse events occurred.
These preliminary findings suggest that continuous acupuncture spanning pretreatment and ovulation induction may be associated with a higher live-birth rate and improvements in metabolic and endometrial parameters. Given the exploratory nature and limited sample size of this pilot trial, confirmation in larger multicenter trials is required.

papers.title: Exploring the therapeutic role of Chinses herbal medicine in the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after conservative surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Liu Z, Liu Y, Li S, Zhang X, Qiang R, Jin F et al.
papers.abstract:
Since surgery can only remove lesions of a larger size visible to the naked eye, the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery is high. In recent years, numerous scholars have found that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment is effective in reducing the recurrence rate of postoperative fibroids, as well as improving the clinical treatment rate, regulating serum hormone levels, reducing plasma viscosity, and promoting the restoration of uterine volume following surgery. Several randomized controlled trials have been undertaken on the prevention and treatment of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids using patented Chinese medicines and self-proposed formulations, such as Guizhi Fuling Pill, Xiaozheng decoction, Xiangleng pill, Zhengjia decoction, Xiaoliu decoction, Guizhi Jiliu pill, Huoxue Huayu formula, Huoxue Xiaozheng decoction, Shugan Sanjie decoction, Gongliuxiao capsule, Hongjin Xiaojie concentrated pill, and Jiawei Guizhi Fuling decoction. However, no study has systematically evaluated Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) in reducing the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery.
This study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of CHM for the prevention of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids, evaluating its efficacy and safety.
A comprehensive search was conducted on PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Information Database (VIP), WanFang Database, and China Biomedical Database (CBM) to identify randomized controlled clinical studies conducted up to March 2025 that examined the efficacy of CHM in treating patients with postoperative uterine fibroids. Two institutes were independently under-selected, and data were extracted and quality assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager software 5.4, and forest plots were generated. The quality of evidence was assessed using GRADEpro 3.2.2. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251000288).
16 trials were included in this study, and the postoperative recurrence rate after treatment was mainly analyzed. CHM treatment reduces postoperative recurrence rates in patients with uterine fibroids compared to the blank (6 trials, n = 588; OR (odds ratio) = 0.22; 95 % CI (95 % confidence intervals) = 0.14-0.34; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001), conventional western medicine (CWM) (1 trial, n = 80; OR = 0.30; 95 % CI = 0.09-0.93, p = 0.04), and combined CHM with CWM (9 trials, n = 959; OR = 0.29; 95 % CI = 0.19-0.46; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001). In addition, CHM is also effective in improving clinical efficiency, restoring serum sex hormone levels, lowering plasma viscosity, and reducing uterine volume. CHM is generally considered safe, with a low incidence of adverse reactions.
CHM is effective in avoiding recurrence of uterine fibroids after surgery, excelling in terms of overall effectiveness, restoring female hormone levels, improving hemorheological indices, and promoting uterine recovery and safety. However, these findings are preliminary and still need to be validated by higher-quality studies.

papers.title: Network pharmacology-based identification and experimental validation of active compounds from Qingda Granules against Ang II-induced hypertension.
papers.journal: Biochemistry and biophysics reports
papers.authors: Zhang L, Ali F, Wu M, Guo Z, Lin G, Zhang X et al.
papers.abstract:
Hypertension is a significant global health issue that raises the risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Qingda Granule (QDG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used to treat hypertension, but its active compounds and mechanisms of action remain poorly understood.
Network pharmacology identified potential active compounds and KEGG pathways. Four compounds-gastrodin, rhynchophylline, baicalin, and liensinine were selected. Hypertension was induced in mice via Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion. QDG (1145 mg/kg/day) or each compound (10 mg/kg/day) was administered orally once daily. Outcomes measured included systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), pulse wave velocity (PWV), and abdominal aortic wall thickness. Histological examination and immunohistochemistry for expression of total myosin light chain (MLC) and phosphorylation of myosin light chain (p-MLC) were performed in exploratory subgroups of three mice per group.
Network pharmacology analysis identified 482 predicted targets overlapping with hypertension-related targets. The compound-target network was constructed and analyzed, and hub nodes were identified using multiple parameters, such as betweenness centrality and degree. These four selected compounds-gastrodin, rhynchophylline, baicalin, and liensinine-ranked among the top 50 nodes in the compound-target network. Consequently, these four compounds were selected for further validation. KEGG enrichment analysis identified vascular smooth muscle contraction as an enriched candidate pathway (18 targets). In vivo, QDG and all four compounds treatment significantly lowered blood pressure, lowered PWV, and reduced abdominal aortic wall thickness. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed attenuated aortic histopathological changes and reduced p-MLC immunoreactivity, with no significant difference in total MLC immunoreactivity in abdominal aortic tissues of Ang II-infused mice.
QDG and its four individually administered compounds attenuated blood pressure elevation and were associated with lower PWV and reduced abdominal aortic wall thickening in Ang II-infused mice, as well as reduced p-MLC immunoreactivity. These findings suggest that the QDG and its four compounds contribute to antihypertensive effects.

papers.title: Response surface optimisation of Xiaoyao San polyphenols and anti-inflammatory activity in colonic epithelial cells.
papers.journal: Natural product research
papers.authors: Huang YX, Que ZQ, Cheng Y, Zheng FP, Chen XQ
papers.abstract: Xiaoyao San is a traditional Chinese medicine formula, but its polyphenol extraction and intestinal epithelial activity remain insufficiently defined. We optimised ethanol-reflux extraction by response surface methodology and evaluated the polyphenol-rich fraction in NCM460 cells. The validated optimum was 57% ethanol, a 7.6 mL/g liquid-solid ratio, and 94 min, yielding 7.44 ± 0.15 mg gallic acid equivalents per gram. Xiaoyao San increased cell viability and proliferation, reduced apoptosis and nitrite accumulation, and decreased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 concentrations. Molecular docking predicted favourable interactions between selected polyphenols and NLRP3, while immunoblotting showed lower NLRP3, caspase-1, and ASC abundance after treatment. The low concentration frequently produced equal or greater effects than the high concentration. These findings connect extraction optimisation with epithelial protection and support chemical standardisation, direct target-engagement studies.

papers.title: Effect of YiFei SanJie Formula on persistent pure ground-glass nodules: a multicenter prospective cohort study.
papers.journal: MedScience
papers.authors: Li J, Zhou M, Han W, Jiao L, Liu Y, Guo W et al.
papers.abstract: Persistent pure ground-glass nodules (pGGNs) are one of the main imaging manifestations of early-stage lung cancer. However, there is a lack of effective treatment methods except surgical resection. To assess the effectiveness of YiFei SanJie Formula (YFSJF) on pGGNs, we conducted a multicenter prospective cohort study. This study was conducted in four centers in China. The clinical efficacy difference between the YFSJF group and non-YFSJF treatment was compared during the 2-year follow-up. The primary outcome was growth rate. The secondary outcomes included regression rate, volume of pGGN, maximum diameter of pGGN in axial plane, and mean CT attenuation of pGGN in axial plane. From January 2021 to December 2022, 63 patients dropped out. Ultimately, 717 patients (91.9%) were included in the final analysis. After 2-year follow-up, pGGN growth was observed in 27 patients (7.2%) in the YFSJF group, compared to 48 patients (14%) in the non-YFSJF (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.29-0.79; P = 0.004). pGGN regression was observed in 27 patients (7.2%) in the YFSJF group, compared to 13 patients (3.8%) in the non-YFSJF group (OR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.15-4.65; P = 0.019). In the multivariable analysis, the YFSJF group had a significant effect on the volume change of pGGNs compared with the non-YFSJF group (P < 0.001). However, maximum diameter and mean CT attenuation did not significantly differ between the two groups (P > 0.05). During the 2-year follow-up period, YFSJF may have a certain effect on pGGNs, which can delay the growth of pGGNs and improve the regression.

papers.title: Isoformononetin alleviates depression through regulating neuroinflammation and mitochondrial homeostasis by targeting PDE4D.
papers.journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
papers.authors: Chu H, Zheng Y, Zheng S, Zhang Y, Kong L, Zhang H
papers.abstract: Depression is a common neuropsychiatric illness characterized by reduced energy, decreased interest or pleasure in activities and persistent feelings of sadness, causing severe burden on both patients and society as its continuously rising incidence, underscoring an urgent need for developing novel antidepressants. Danggui Buxue Decoction (DBD) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula traditionally indicated for deficiency patterns. However, whether DBD can alleviate depression, the bioactive constituents and molecular basis remain unexplored. Here, we evaluated the antidepression activities of DBD and identified isoformononetin (IFM) as the key bioactive constituent in chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced mouse model. IFM ameliorated depressive‑like behaviors and hippocampal tissue damages induced by CUMS, while increased serum levels of 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT). Mechanistically, IFM bound to phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D) protein and promoted its ubiquitination-dependent degradation, thereby activating the cAMP-CREB-BDNF signaling axis and regulating mitochondrial homeostasis. Moreover, IFM ameliorated neuroinflammation via reducing NOD-like receptor thermal protein domain associated protein 3 (NLRP3) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Collectively, our findings unveil an unpublished mechanism by which the phytochemical IFM exerts neuroprotective and anti‑inflammatory effects, positioning IFM as a potential antidepressant agent and laying the groundwork for the development of innovative clinical treatment approaches.

papers.title: Astragaloside IV-Loaded PRP-Exosomes Promote Angiogenic Functions in HUVECs: Association with Jagged-1/Notch Pathway Activation.
papers.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
papers.authors: Wu J, Chen B, Fang R, Zhu Z, Yang X, Suo Y
papers.abstract:
Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) exhibits prominent pro-angiogenic activity. Platelet-rich plasma-derived exosomes (PRP-Exos) serve as natural nanocarriers with intrinsic tissue-repairing activity. This study aimed to construct AS-IV-loaded PRP-Exos (AS-IV/PRP-Exos) and investigate their combined regulatory effects on the functions of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs).
PRP-Exos were extracted by ultracentrifugation and characterized by western blot, transmission electron microscopy, and nanoparticle tracking analysis. AS-IV was loaded into PRP-Exos via sonication, and the encapsulation efficiency was determined by high-performance liquid chromatography. The cellular uptake of PKH67-labeled exosomes by HUVECs was observed via fluorescence microscopy. A high-glucose-induced HUVEC injury model was established, and cells were treated with AS-IV, PRP-Exos, or AS-IV/PRP-Exos to assess cell viability, migration, and tube formation. The expression of angiogenesis-related and Notch pathway molecules was detected by RT-qPCR and Western blot. Finally, exogenous Jagged-1 was introduced as an intervention to observe its effects.
The extracted PRP-Exos exhibited typical exosomal morphology, with an AS-IV encapsulation efficiency of 49.82%, and were effectively internalized by HUVECs. Compared with AS-IV or PRP-Exos monotherapy, AS-IV/PRP-Exos significantly enhanced HUVEC viability, migration, and tube formation. Mechanistically, AS-IV/PRP-Exos downregulated the expression of VEGF and DLL4, while upregulating the expression of CD31, E-cadherin, and Jagged-1. Additionally, AS-IV/PRP-Exos elevated cleaved Notch1, Hes1, and Hey1 expression. Importantly, exogenous Jagged-1 reversed these effects and attenuated the functional improvements induced by AS-IV/PRP-Exos.
This study provides experimental evidence for the combined application of active ingredients from traditional Chinese medicine and exosome-based delivery system.
