papers.title: Protective Effects of the Standardized Extract of Amburana cearensis in an Experimental Model of Severe Asthma: Suppression of Airway Inflammation and Modulation of Neutrophil Function.
papers.journal: Advances in pharmacological and pharmaceutical sciences
papers.authors: Amaral HHS, Rocha TM, Araújo EVO, de Araújo AB, Bezerra AME, Evangelista JSAM et al.
papers.abstract: Amburana cearensis A.C. Smith (Fabaceae) is traditionally used in Brazilian medicine for the treatment of asthma; however, its effects in experimental models of asthma exacerbation remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of a standardized dried extract of A. cearensis (DEAC) and its chemical constituents-coumarin (CM) and vanillic acid (VA)-on airway inflammation in a murine model of ovalbumin (OVA) + lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced asthma exacerbation and on human neutrophil activation. DEAC was characterized by high-performance liquid chromatography with photodiode array detection (HPLC-PDA) (markers: CM, VA, and amburoside). BALB/c mice were sensitized and challenged with OVA + LPS and treated with DEAC (100 mg/kg) and CM. On Day 26, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and lungs were analyzed for total and differential leukocytes, cytokines interleukin-4 (IL-4) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and histopathological changes. The effects of DEAC, CM, and VA on phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced human neutrophil activation were assessed through myeloperoxidase release and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production by chemiluminescence. OVA + LPS challenge induced severe airway inflammation, characterized by increased leukocyte recruitment, predominance of neutrophils, elevated IL-4 and TNF-α levels, and mucus hypersecretion. DEAC markedly reduced total leukocyte accumulation, restored the mononuclear cell proportion, and decreased neutrophil and eosinophil infiltration, with effects comparable to dexamethasone. CM reduced neutrophil accumulation without affecting total leukocytes. Lung histology confirmed decreased inflammation and mucus production. DEAC also lowered IL-4 and TNF-α levels. DEAC, CM, and VA inhibited neutrophil degranulation and ROS generation without affecting cell viability. These findings demonstrate the anti-inflammatory potential of A. cearensis and support its traditional use as an adjuvant therapy for asthma within Brazilian public phytotherapy programs.

summary.methods: OVA+LPS로 유도한 생쥐 천식 악화 모델과 PMA로 활성화한 사람 호중구를 이용해, DEAC와 성분인 쿠마린 및 바닐릭산의 염증 및 호중구 기능 변화를 평가했다.

papers.title: Fabrication of carbon dots derived from Alangium salviifolium for the sequential sensing Ag+ and S2- and further monitoring of H2S in spoiled food.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Qi X, Yang H, Xu D, Cui T, Dai Q, Chen G et al.
papers.abstract: Given the significant threat posed by heavy metals to ecological system and human health, the development of precise, portable, and on-site analytical technologies is urgently required. Herein, multifunctional carbon dots (A-CDs) derived from the traditional chinese medicine (TCM) were synthesized and exhibited optimal emission at 604 nm excited at 495 nm, with quantum yield (QY) of 18.25%. The A-CDs achieved the cascade determination of Ag+ and S2- via a subsequent "on-off-on" process with LODs of 63.7 nM and 0.98 μM, respectively. Notably, A-CDs portable platform was constructed and enabled on-site quantitative analysis with LODs of 0.83 μM and 1.19 μM, respectively. Leveraging this unique sensing performance, the A-CDs test strips were developed for visual screening of H2S during food spoilage at varying storage temperatures, allowing qualitative food freshness discrimination via naked-eye observation. The precise quantitative detection in real water and foodstuff was applied, and further verified by ICP-MS, confirmed the excellent accuracy and environmental tolerance. This work presented an intelligent strategy for designing cost-effective, high-performance multivariate probes, holding significant promise for advancing food safety and environmental monitoring.

papers.title: A dual-signal sensor for highly selective and reliable detection of rutin based on molecularly imprinted Prussian blue analogue.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Xu J, Wang H, Bai H, Li J, Li H, Ma D
papers.abstract: The reliable and accurate quantification of rutin is essential for pharmaceutical quality control, pharmacokinetic investigations, and clinical applications, owing to its broad pharmacological activities. In this study, we address this need by developing a novel dual-mode sensing platform based on a molecularly imprinted polymer-coated bimetallic Prussian blue analogue (Mn/FePBA@MIP). The Mn/FePBA@MIP analogue not only exhibits high peroxidase-like catalytic activity via its synergistic bimetallic sites but also possesses target-specific recognition capability through its surface-imprinted cavities. Upon specific rebinding of rutin, the imprinted polymer layer blocks substrate access to the catalytic sites via a gatekeeper effect, thereby quenching both the colorimetric and fluorescent signals. Under optimized conditions, the developed sensor achieves wide linear detection ranges of 6-1536 μg mL-1 for the colorimetric mode and 6-3072 μg mL-1 for the fluorescent mode, with corresponding detection limits of 3.98 μg mL-1 and 1.32 μg mL-1, respectively. For on-site applications, the sensor was integrated with a smartphone-based readout system for quantitative analysis via RGB value extraction, and successfully applied to determine rutin in traditional Chinese medicine samples with satisfactory recoveries. This work thus provides a reliable and portable dual-signal strategy for routine quality assurance of rutin-related herbal products.

papers.title: Research on the composition of total flavonoid aglycones in Clematis aethusifolia Turcz. and its effects on HaCaT cells and melanin.
papers.journal: Natural product research
papers.authors: Longwei F, La Y, Zhuoma D, Parbeen S, Hebing X, Jie L et al.
papers.abstract: Solar dermatitis is driven by UV-induced oxidative stress and pigmentation disorders. Clematis aethusifolia Turcz., a traditional Chinese medicine used empirically for solar dermatitis and melasma, lacks mechanistic understanding. This study characterised its flavonoid aglycones and evaluated their photoprotective and anti-melanogenic effects. High‑performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) identified quercetin, kaempferol, luteolin and apigenin as major aglycones. The flavonoids (≤80 μg/mL) were non-cytotoxic to human immortalized keratinocytes (HaCaT) cells (>95% viability). At 5-45 μg/mL, they dose-dependently attenuated UVB-induced damage, raising cell viability from 68.54% (UVB control) to 92.45%. CAT exhibited cell selectivity against melanoma cell lines, displaying potent inhibition against A375 cells but weaker activity against B16F10 cells than arbutin. Molecular docking revealed quercetin had the strongest binding to interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and tyrosinase (TYR). These findings demonstrate that total flavonoids from C. aethusifolia mitigate UVB-induced skin damage and inhibit melanogenesis, supporting their potential for treating UV-related dermatoses.

papers.title: S-propargyl-L-cysteine attenuates ketamine induced schizophrenia-like behaviors and neuroinflammation in mice via inhibition of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis.
papers.journal: International immunopharmacology
papers.authors: Wang H, Huang Y, Hu Q, Zhang F, Wang Z, Zeng J et al.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a serious neuropsychiatric disorder with a complex etiology. Neuroinflammation has received much attention as a crucial contributor to the pathogenesis of SCZ. S-propargyl-L-cysteine (SPRC), a synthesized analog of S-allyl-L-cysteine, increases endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H2S) synthesis and exerts potent antioxidative and anti-inflammatory effects. However, its potential role in SCZ-related neuroinflammation remains unclear. The aim of the present study was to investigate whether SPRC protects against ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like symptoms and to explore underlying mechanisms related to cystathionine-γ-lyase (CSE)/H2S signaling and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) activation. Behavioral alterations were assessed using the open-field test, Y-maze test, and prepulse inhibition analysis. Neuronal damage in the hippocampus was evaluated using Nissl staining, while changes in the CSE/H2S pathway, mature brain-derived neurotrophic factor (mBDNF), inflammatory pathways, and pyroptosis pathway were also analyzed. SPRC was found to effectively reverse ketamine-induced hyperactivity and anxiety, as well as improve working memory and sensorimotor gating defects. Furthermore, SPRC prevented neuronal loss across the hippocampal CA1, CA3, and dentate gyrus subregions. The mechanism of action involves the reversal of CSE activity and H2S production, maintenance of mBDNF, as well as the suppression of NF-κB translocation. This is also characterized by reduction in tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) production. Additionally, SPRC inhibited nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, caspase-1-mediated pyroptosis, and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) secretion. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that SPRC alleviates ketamine-induced behavioral deficits and neuroinflammation in mice, likely via restoration of the CSE/ H2S pathway and suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis.

papers.title: Chemical Characterization and Mechanism Analysis of Ganjianglingzhu Decoction in the Treatment of Low Back Pain Based on UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS and Network Pharmacology.
papers.journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM
papers.authors: Chen B, Li P, Shi J, Xu F, Sun S
papers.abstract:
Ganjianglingzhu decoction (GJLZD), a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula, has been widely used in the treatment of low back pain. However, its chemical composition and underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently elucidated.
The chemical profile of GJLZD was comprehensively characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS. Representative bioactive constituents were subsequently selected for target prediction using the PharmMapper and SwissTargetPrediction databases. Overlapping targets between compound-related targets and low back pain-related targets retrieved from the GeneCards database were subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, Gene Ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, as well as molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation.
Based on MS/MS fragmentation patterns and literature comparison, a total of 58 constituents were tentatively characterized from GJLZD. These mainly included flavonoids, alkaloids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids. We identified 466 overlapping targets between the active components and low back pain. PPI analysis highlighted SRC, PIK3CA, and AKT1 as the major hub targets. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses suggested that these targets were primarily involved in signal transduction, inflammatory regulation, and metabolism. The enriched pathways included VEGF, FcεRI, and AGE-RAGE signaling. Molecular docking revealed that neoglycyrol showed the strongest binding affinity to AKT1, with a binding energy of -7.93 kcal/mol. MD simulation further confirmed the stability of the neoglycyrol-AKT1 complex over 100 ns.
This study systematically characterized the chemical constituents of GJLZD and elucidated its potential mechanisms in treating low back pain. The results suggest a multicomponent and multi-target mode of action. The integrated strategy combining UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS with network pharmacology and molecular simulations proved valuable for investigating the pharmacological basis of TCM formulas. Further experimental validation is still needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Authentication of the Botanical Origins of Curcumae Radix Based on DNA Barcoding and HS-GC-IMS.
papers.journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM
papers.authors: Jiang Q, Yin J, Han X, Yong J, Sun R, Liu M et al.
papers.abstract:
As a classic multiorigin herbal medicine, the precise authentication of Curcumae Radix (Yujin) is crucial for ensuring market standardization and clinical efficacy. Given the complexity of herbal materials, single-method identification often lacks the resolution required to distinguish between closely related species or handle degraded with significant DNA degradation.
A two-dimensional analytical strategy was applied to 24 batches of Curcumae Radix samples. This approach combined ITS2 DNA barcoding for genetic identification with headspace gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (HS-GC-IMS) to analyze volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles. The resulting HS-GC-IMS data were processed using chemometric tools, including principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), to compare and differentiate the decoction pieces.
The results demonstrated that while ITS2 DNA barcoding effectively identified Curcuma kwangsiensis S. G. Lee et C. F. Liang, it failed to discriminate between the closely related species Curcuma longa L. and Curcuma phaeocaulis Val. and was ineffective for DNA-degraded samples of Curcuma wenyujin Y. H. Chen et C. Ling. Conversely, HS-GC-IMS successfully established distinct VOC fingerprints for each source. When coupled with chemometric analysis, this method pinpointed specific interspecific discriminatory biomarkers that allowed for clear differentiation where genetic barcoding fell short.
By integrating stable genetic information with volatile chemical fingerprints, this study establishes a complementary two-dimensional identification system. This strategy provides an innovative and reliable solution for the botanical authentication and quality control of Curcumae Radix, offering a broadly applicable paradigm for the precise identification of other complex herbal materials.

papers.title: Acupuncture-Assisted Zolpidem Tartrate Tapering and Discontinuation in Patients with Chronic Insomnia Disorder Stabilized on Zolpidem: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: Nature and science of sleep
papers.authors: Liu L, Guo Z, Jiang S, Yang M, Zhang Y, Hu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
The prevalence of chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is relatively high and increases with age. The use of sedatives, along with the incidence of their adverse effects, is also rising, which can easily lead to health risks and negative outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of acupuncture-assisted zolpidem tartrate tapering and discontinuation in patients with CID whose insomnia symptoms are clinically stable while taking zolpidem.
This study is designed as a single-center, single-blind, randomized controlled trial.Ninety participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the acupuncture group or the sham acupuncture group. Each participant will undergo 24 sessions of either acupuncture or sham acupuncture, in conjunction with zolpidem tartrate tapering therapy, over a duration of 8 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up observation period. The primary outcome is the discontinuation rate of zolpidem tartrate at week 8. Secondary outcomes include the reduction rate of zolpidem tartrate, the discontinuation rates at weeks 10 and 12, frequency of zolpidem tartrate use (nights/week), average daily dose (mg/day), total weekly dose (mg/week), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Generalized Anxiety Disorder -7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), Short Form Health Survey-12 (SF-12), sleep diary-related indicators, Dysfunctional Beliefs and Attitudes about Sleep Scale -16 (DBAS-16), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and emergency medication usage. Adverse events will also be monitored throughout the study. Efficacy analyses will be conducted on the intention-to-treat population.
The findings of the study may provide preliminary evidence for standardized protocols for reducing and ceasing zolpidem tartrate use through acupuncture assistance. Additionally, this research may offer useful references for patients with CID seeking to safely and effectively reduce or discontinue zolpidem tartrate. These findings may inform future clinical research and larger multicenter confirmatory studies.

papers.title: An integrated UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS strategy for comprehensive characterization of chemical constituents and in vivo metabolic profile of Bupi Yichang pills.
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.authors: Han Y, Li H, Chen C, Xie Y, Xu K, Zhu F et al.
papers.abstract: Bupi Yichang Pills (BYP) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) prescription used for spleen-deficiency diarrhea and chronic colitis, yet its pharmacodynamic material basis remains unclear. This study employed UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS to comprehensively characterize the chemical constituents of BYP in vitro and to identify prototype compounds and metabolites in rat plasma, urine, bile, feces, and tissues. In total, 183 compounds were identified in vitro, predominantly flavonoids, triterpenoid saponins, monoterpene glycosides, chromones, and coumarins. Based on this library, 93 prototype compounds and 98 metabolites were detected in vivo. Tissue distribution showed the largest numbers of compounds in the colon, ileum, and spleen. Flavonoids and monoterpene glycosides were the most frequently detected classes. Calycosin, paeoniflorin, and their metabolites were detected in the brain. These results indicate that the identified chemical classes are the major components detected in vivo in BYP and may serve as the candidate material basis for its efficacy, providing a scientific foundation for quality control marker selection, mechanism studies, and clinical application.

papers.title: Preserved tendon reflexes in a clinically suspected sensory-predominant GBS-spectrum disorder: a case report.
papers.journal: Journal of medical case reports
papers.authors: Min X, Liu W, Wang R, Yang X, Ke T, Zhang W et al.
papers.abstract:
Guillain-Barré syndrome usually comes to clinical attention because of progressive weakness and reduced or absent tendon reflexes. Some patients, however, present mainly with sensory symptoms and still have preserved reflexes, making early diagnosis more difficult.
A 71-year-old Han Chinese man presented with distal paresthesia after an episode of diarrhea, and the symptoms became noticeably worse over the next 2 days. The sensory disturbance spread in a glove-and-sock pattern and was accompanied by heaviness in the legs, difficulty walking, and mild distal weakness. Neurological examination showed reduced distal superficial sensation, preserved tendon reflexes, and no pathological reflexes. Brain MRI showed no clinically relevant abnormality, and spinal MRI showed degenerative changes without a definite central lesion explaining the symptoms. Cerebrospinal fluid showed protein of 590 mg/L with a reported white blood cell count of 0.001 × 106/L, a pattern compatible with albuminocytologic dissociation. Because nerve conduction studies and electromyography were not completed during hospitalization, the diagnosis remained a clinically suspected sensory-predominant disorder within the GBS spectrum rather than electrophysiologically confirmed classic GBS. Clinical notes recorded improvement during hospitalization, and the patient regained independent ambulation after receiving intravenous immunoglobulin alongside supportive and adjunctive therapies. At a telephone follow-up approximately 12 months later, he reported no recurrence; no objective follow-up examination was available.
In patients with acute symmetric distal sensory symptoms after a gastrointestinal illness, preserved tendon reflexes do not by themselves exclude a GBS-spectrum disorder. In this patient, the clinical course and cerebrospinal fluid findings supported consideration of that diagnosis, but the absence of electrophysiological testing precluded confirmation. This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge posed by atypical sensory-predominant presentations and also highlights that, without electrophysiological confirmation, both subtype assignment and overall diagnostic certainty remain constrained.

papers.title: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. stem extract attenuates cigarette smoke-induced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in mice by modulating PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Yang N, Zhai J, Gong J, Zhang Y, Yu L, Wang C et al.
papers.abstract:
Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. (COT) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its root, stem, and leaf being used for medicinal purposes. COT characterized by the efficacy of dispelling wind-dampness, invigorating blood, and relieving pain, traditional records in Quanzhou Bencao document the use for asthma, indicating that its traditional treatment in lung system disorders. Previous pharmacological studies have demonstrated that the COT stem (COTS) exhibits anti-inflammatory and protective effects in experimental models related to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the systemically efficacy and molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-COPD effects of COTS remain poorly understood.
The purpose of this study is to systematically investigate the therapeutic efficacy of the extract of COTS (ECOTS) against COPD in mice through metabolomics and serum pharmacochemistry combined with network pharmacology, thereby providing experimental evidence for elucidating the underlying mechanisms through which ECOTS exerts its therapeutic effects on COPD.
Cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD-like mouse model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects of ECOTS. The potential biomarkers were identified by metabolomics. The blood-entering components were profiled by serum pharmacochemistry. The primary targets and signaling pathways of ECOTS were predicted through network pharmacology analysis. These predictions were further validated using immunohistochemical, immunofluorescence, and Western blot.
ECOTS significantly suppressed inflammation and mitigated lung tissue damage in CS-induced mice. Network pharmacology screening and verification experiments revealed that the protective effects of ECOTS may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling in vivo and in vitro. Furthermore, the PI3K agonist 740 Y-P apparently impaired the effects of ECOTS in CS extract (CSE)-exposed BEAS-2B cells.
ECOTS attenuates CS-induced COPD-like pathological changes in mice, and these protective effects may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling. This study extends previous evidence for the anti-COPD activity of the COTS and provides a potential mechanistic and pharmacological basis for its further investigation in COPD.

summary.limitations: 마우스와 세포 실험 중심 연구로 인간 COPD에 대한 유효성과 안전성은 확인되지 않았다.

papers.title: Development of a Case Report Form and Practice-Based Research Network Pilot Registry for Health-Promoting Herbal Medicine in Korean Medicine Clinics.
papers.journal: Complementary therapies in medicine
papers.authors: Jang S, Cheon C, Jegal KH, Yang C, Kim S
papers.abstract:
Herbal medicine (HM) for health promotion is a growing practice in Korean medicine (KM) outpatient settings, yet standardized outcome measurement frameworks tailored to this context remain lacking. This study aimed to develop a standardized case report form (CRF) for health-promoting HM and to describe the clinical effectiveness of individualized HM prescriptions across key health domains in patients seeking health promotion care within a practice-based research network (PBRN).
The CRF was developed through a four-phase process: domain selection, expert and clinician review, pilot feasibility testing, and iterative refinement, yielding a two-tier instrument incorporating five validated patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). The CRF was then deployed in a prospective, observational, multicenter registry across 13 KM clinics, and pre- and post-treatment outcomes were compared using paired t-tests.
A two-tier CRF with five validated PROMs was finalized and deployed within the PBRN. Of 100 enrolled participants who received HM for health promotion, 39 completed both assessments. Statistically significant improvements were observed in four of five symptom domains - sleep discomfort, psychological stress, digestive discomfort, and urinary discomfort (all p<0.05) - while fatigue showed a non-significant trend toward improvement.
This study demonstrates the feasibility of developing and deploying a standardized CRF within a community-based KM PBRN. Preliminary, hypothesis-generating observations suggest potential symptom-level improvement across multiple functional domains; however, given the small per-protocol sample, absence of a control group, and heterogeneity across sites and concomitant treatments, these findings should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in larger, controlled studies.

papers.title: Association of midbrain IL-6 with impaired nest-building behavior and therapeutic effect of Ninjin'yoeito in old hindlimb-unloading mice.
papers.journal: Neuroscience letters
papers.authors: Matsubara Y, Mizuno K, Yakabe M, Ogawa S
papers.abstract: Psychiatric symptoms can substantially impact rehabilitation outcomes in older patients with disuse syndrome. However, the mechanisms underlying these psychiatric symptoms remain poorly understood, and no established treatment is currently available. This study used hindlimb unloading (HU) as a model of disuse syndrome in old male mice to evaluate the effects of Ninjin'yoeito (NYT), a traditional Japanese herbal medicine. After 2 weeks of HU, old mice underwent the nest building test to evaluate goal-directed behavior, and the open field and elevated plus maze tests to assess anxiety-like behavior. Compared to age-matched sham mice, HU-subjected mice showed declines in nest building and locomotor activity but no appreciable anxiety-like behavior during reloading period. Seven days after HU, IL-6 expression was elevated in the midbrain and was co-expressed with microglia in the ventral tegmental area (VTA). In young mice, intra-VTA injection of IL-6 impaired nest building behavior. In activated primary microglial cultures, NYT reduced IL-6 mRNA expression. During recovery from HU, repeated NYT administration improved nest building and motor function while reducing midbrain IL-6 protein levels in old mice. These findings suggest that elevated IL-6 expression in midbrain/VTA is associated with the impairment of goal-directed behavior after HU and that this impairment can be attenuated by NYT. Collectively, these preclinical findings suggest that pharmacological intervention may provide a therapeutic approach for psychiatric-like behavioral changes associated with disuse syndrome.

papers.title: Effects of acupuncture on cognitive function and brain activation in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Complementary therapies in clinical practice
papers.authors: Gong J, Chong Y, Li M, Ma Q, Wu Q, Sun J et al.
papers.abstract:
Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) may represent an important window for interventions to delay dementia progression. Acupuncture, a central practice of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), has been studied as a non-pharmacological approach for MCI; however, clinical and neurofunctional evidence supporting its efficacy remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the effects of acupuncture on cognitive function and brain activation in older adults with MCI.
In this randomized, assessor-blinded, controlled trial, 60 older adults with MCI were assigned to an experimental group receiving 12 weeks of acupuncture plus health education or a control group receiving health education alone. Cognitive assessments, including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Shape Trail Test parts A and B (STT-A and STT-B), along with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measurements during a verbal fluency task (VFT), were performed at baseline and after 12 weeks. Task-related β-values in seven regions of interest (ROIs), such as the frontal pole area (FPA), temporal cortex (TC), and Broca's area, were analyzed.
Among the 60 randomized participants, 56 (27 in the experimental group, 29 in the control group) completed the trial and were included in the primary analysis. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for baseline scores, revealed a significantly greater improvement in MoCA scores for the experimental group (adjusted mean difference = 4.66, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.76-5.55, P < 0.001), along with greater reductions in STT-A (-11.83 s, P = 0.007) and STT-B (-40.86 s, P = 0.003). fNIRS analysis indicated significant time-by-group interactions in the FPA, TC, and Broca's area (P < 0.05), with β-values increasing exclusively in the experimental group. Cognitive improvements correlated with β-value changes in TC (r = 0.30, P = 0.029) and Broca's area (r = 0.34, P = 0.011).
Acupuncture may improve cognitive function in older adults with MCI, accompanied by an increase in task-related β-values in the temporal cortex and Broca's area.
